misuse.support: Deliberate malicious uses and harmful objectives, distinct from accidental errors.

mis-disinformation.support: AI-generated false information, human judgement and pollution of information systems.

hate-unfairness.summary: Identity-based hostility, demeaning representations or discriminatory treatment generated or reinforced by AI systems.
hate-unfairness.support: Toxicity and discrimination combined with documented bias and fairness concepts.

security.support: AI-system compromise, adversarial manipulation and attacks bypassing safeguards.

human-rights.support: Rights and freedoms as normative standards, complemented by AI discrimination, privacy and access harms.

out-of-control.support: Loss of effective human control and incentives affecting interruptibility.

prompt-injection.support: Untrusted inputs redirecting instructions and tool-integrated agents.

human-robot-interaction.support: The HRI textbook supports interaction design, communication and coordination; the teleoperation survey supports a concrete form of human-robot collaboration.

general-ai.support: Broadly adaptable digital-content models. HEART's General AI domain is an operational taxonomy definition, not equivalent to AGI.

agentic-ai.support: Autonomous agents, planning, reasoning and tool-mediated actions.

physical-ai.support: Embodied perception and action in environments, including physical robots.

agi.support: Generality and performance across cognitive tasks; these papers do not establish that current systems have achieved AGI.

asi.support: Superhuman breadth and performance; a conceptual capability level, not a claim of an existing deployed system.

humanoid.support: Human-like robot embodiments with locomotion, manipulation and teleoperation capabilities.

fairness.support: Context-dependent fairness criteria, equitable access and distributions of benefits and harms.

deepfake.support: Generative manipulation of identity and audiovisual content that can appear authentic.

copyrights.support: Copyright implications of training and substantially similar outputs; extraction is technical evidence, not a legal determination of infringement.

ai-for-everyone.summary: Korea's planned citizen-facing AI services combine general-purpose chatbots with agents for information search, applications, bookings and payments. Relevant risks depend on the capabilities enabled. The English label is a descriptive translation, not a verified official programme name.
ai-for-everyone.support: Yonhap supports programme-specific facts; the foundation-model report and agent survey support general digital-content capabilities and agent architecture only, not evidence about this programme.

legal-assistance.summary: AI supporting legal intake, document review, legal research and drafting under qualified human supervision. Relevant risks include inaccurate legal information, confidentiality breaches, biased access and inadequate traceability. Assistance is distinct from autonomous adjudication or replacing a lawyer.
legal-assistance.support: Scoped legal-help prototypes and empirical evidence of legal hallucinations.

financial-chatbots.summary: Conversational AI providing consumer-facing explanations and guidance about financial products and decisions. Relevant risks include misleading information, unsuitable guidance, disclosure of personal financial data and unclear responsibility. This lens does not assume autonomous trading or regulated personalised advice.
financial-chatbots.support: FCA pilots distinguish financial guidance from advice; the CFPB report addresses deficient responses, privacy and consumer-protection risks in financial chatbots.
